notes.text: Jonathan Aspirot has not dressed for the last 5 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Frédéric Brunet has taken his spot beside Mason Lohrei.
Sean Kuraly has not dressed for the last 5 games. Matthew Poitras has taken his spot beside Tanner Jeannot and Mark Kastelic.
Connor Clifton returned in their last game after missing 7 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Trevor van Riemsdyk is day to day (lower body injury) and has missed the last 8 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Spencer Stastney has taken his spot beside Kris Letang.
Evgeni Malkin is out (illness), reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-six forward.
Bryan Rust is on injured reserve and has missed the last 3 games. Tommy Novak has taken his spot beside Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell.
Egor Chinakhov returned in their last game after missing 2 games.
Ilya Solovyov was added to the roster on Oct 20 and has played beside Kris Letang.
Rutger McGroarty was added to the roster on Oct 23 and has played beside Blake Lizotte and Andrei Kuzmenko.
Avery Hayes was added to the roster on Oct 25 and has played beside Hendrix Lapierre and Ville Koivunen.
Ilya Solovyov has started killing penalties: on the ice for 43% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, up from 5% last season.
Spencer Stastney is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 8 games, down from 31% with his old team last season.

PIT.head: The Penguins should have the upper hand
PIT.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Pittsburgh has home-ice advantage and gets Solovyov back. The Bruins’ way back in is getting good looks.

BOS.head: A tough matchup for the Bruins
BOS.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Pittsburgh has home-ice advantage and gets Solovyov back. The Bruins’ best way through is getting good looks.

story.head: Clifton returns to Pittsburgh
paras: The Bruins (9-4-1) lost 4-1 to St. Louis on Oct 29, and the Penguins (5-6-2) lost 4-3 in overtime to Utah the same night. Going in, the Bruins are first in the Atlantic (tied for fourth in the NHL) and the Pens sixth in the Metropolitan (tied for 24th).

The Bruins’ record (.679) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.555), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Penguins have played better than their record (.462) says: their chances are worth about .559, and losses in one-goal games have held them back. If their records matched their chances, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.

The Penguins (lowest) and the Bruins (2nd lowest) both sit back rather than chase on the forecheck. The Bruins have had the league’s best goaltending (1st). They also leave the shooting to their forwards (lowest), so the Penguins have the edge over them on shots from defensemen. Boston has allowed 2.29 goals a game, the second fewest in the league. As for the Penguins, they get more of their shots from in close than anyone (1st) and rarely throw hits (lowest). The Bruins could find some good looks against the Penguins, who give up plenty of them.

David Pastrňák (7 G / 11 A / 18 P in 14 GP) leads the Bruins in scoring. For the Penguins, Erik Karlsson (2 G / 11 A / 13 P in 13 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Nick Robertson (6 G / 0 A / 6 P in 13 GP) has a team-high six goals.
Jeremy Swayman (7-3-1 / .912 SV% in 11 GS) has been outstanding for Boston and will likely start. Artūrs Šilovs (5-3-1 / .889 SV% in 9 GS) is in line to start for Pittsburgh.
